primary_antecedent.scope: Prescribed superharmonic Sobolev regularity, countable index detection and positive-ray wavefront realization.

source_correspondence: The exact statement retains n at least three, an arbitrary connected planar open set, lower semicontinuity on the whole plane, infinite index outside the closure and possible finite boundary values. It asserts exact positive-ray wavefront, interior index equality and only a boundary lower bound.
Actual rational-ball minimizers detect all lower-semicontinuous upper bounds. Density alone is insufficient; the first solved exercise proves the obstruction using rational downward spikes.

Circle means and radial integration prove local integrability of the negative index. Radial convolution and a small positive quadratic give a smooth strict subharmonic majorant satisfying every finite compact test constraint.

The countable microlocal topology uses actual proper order tests and retains full coarse compact-input Fourier norms. Finite elliptic partitions include their smooth errors; fixed neighborhoods with all Sobolev orders prove smoothness away from the prescribed ray.

Compatible compact Sobolev limits, actual operator continuity and coordinate fundamental-theorem limits prove completeness with every smooth source derivative. No unproved closed-graph estimate replaces this argument.
Localized norm balls are closed by distributional Fourier convergence and Fatou. Interior would give an explicit finite estimate, including the zero-seminorm case and every retained coarse norm.

The full ordinary operator acts on the packet through an actual reduced partial Fourier amplitude. Tangential Taylor remainders, large tangential frequencies, normal amplitude reduction and separated kernels are controlled after every derivative.
The strict conormal L2 threshold and the lower amplitude remainder are proved directly. The lower bound does not infer an amplitude endpoint from an unproved Sobolev converse.

One smooth strict barrier satisfies the finite microlocal tests and the coarse Fourier constraints simultaneously. Delivered holomorphic peaks on an arbitrary open set give one smooth packet at each scale and exact cancellation of the localized source.

All packet derivatives have explicit logarithmic losses absorbed in ordinary symbol classes. The frequency cone is positive, off-plane pieces are uniformly smooth and proper tests retain all lower terms.

Full coarse Fourier norms include their nonlocal output tails. Compact inputs are uniformly bounded distributions; separated multiplier kernels and all derivatives decrease rapidly, proving the omitted tail is uniformly L2.

The target amplitude is bounded below on a planar disk of radius c/log(t) and a normal-frequency ball of radius t/(16 log(t)). Its half-order-smaller remainder preserves the lower bound. Partial Plancherel gives t^(2 gamma)/(log(t))^n, including the exact dimension n=d+2.

Countably many shrinking elliptic tests and the complete-metric Baire theorem select one distribution. The minimizer set extends equality to every interior point; density and closed conicity give the full wavefront set, including the boundary.

The delivered full scalar graph intertwiner transfers the realization to each matched nonradial involutive canonical patch. The conclusion is local and does not assert a global construction across arbitrary canonical charts.

The weighted planar estimates and complex involutive propagation supply the companion proofs for Section 26.2. The positive-packet model gives a separate explicit realization of concave indices on a real characteristic curve.
